method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 44's east margin prints 'AVENUE L' with adjoining sheet no. 45; its last block frontage reads 1113 1115 1117 1119 1121 1123 (side numbers 2202-2228). Sheet 45's west margin prints 'AVENUE L' with adjoining sheet no. 44; its first block frontage reads 1201 1203 1205 1207 1209 1211 (side numbers 2201-2227). The 1100/1200 hundred-block change happens across this corridor. One block west on sheet 44 is the printed 'AVENUE K' (1000/1100 change); one block east on sheet 45 is 'AVENUE M' (1200/1300 change, frontage 1301 1303 1305 1307). Position recorded is the corridor centreline in that sheet's native raster px, obtained by reading the drawn block-face line off the green native-pixel ruler and adding half the corridor width measured on the same sheet (80 ft streets = 241-246 px, 70 ft avenues = 209-214 px, 20 ft alleys = 60 px, all at ~3.0 px/ft).
